# Create Boss (Central AI) gym scene

## Problem statement

Create a Phaser gym scene demonstrating the Boss — "The Central AI" from GDD §4.3. The scene should show its multi-phase health bar, 3–4 distinct attack pattern phases, and complex bullet patterns. This is the final challenge enemy with unique mechanics (multi-hit health, phase transitions).

## Users

- **Player / developer** testing boss behaviour — wants to see all boss attack phases, health bar, and bullet patterns in isolation.
- **AI agents implementing AI_Hell** — need a reference implementation of multi-phase boss behaviour with health bar management.

### Example user stories

- As a **developer**, I want to see the Boss cycle through 3–4 distinct attack pattern phases so I can verify the phase transition logic.
- As a **developer**, I want to see a 4-phase health bar that visually depletes as the Boss takes damage so I can verify the health bar rendering.
- As a **developer**, I want to click a button to deal damage to the Boss so I can test health bar progression and phase transitions.
- As a **developer**, I want to see clear visual and audio cues before each boss attack phase begins so I can verify the telegraphing system.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Gym scene exists:** A Phaser scene (`src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts`) renders the Boss enemy with all attack patterns.
- [ ] **AC2 — Boss visual style:** The Central AI renders as a large, imposing neon entity with a visible central core, consistent with a "boss" aesthetic.
- [ ] **AC3 — Multi-phase health bar:** A 4-phase health bar is displayed; each phase depletes independently. The Boss cycles through 3–4 distinct attack patterns as health phases progress.
- [ ] **AC4 — Boss attack phases implemented:** All Boss phases from the GDD are present:
  - **Phase 1:** Spread — Boss fires bullets in a wide spread pattern.
  - **Phase 2:** Spiral — Bullets spiral outward from the Boss in a rotating pattern.
  - **Phase 3:** Pulse — Screen-wide pulse wave expands from the Boss, followed by aimed shots at the player's last known position.
  - **Phase 4 — Desperation:** All previous patterns combined at higher speed; Boss core becomes more exposed/bright (visual cue).
- [ ] **AC5 — Damage button:** A button on-screen deals damage to the Boss, advancing the health bar through phases. Visual cues (core exposure) change at each phase transition.
- [ ] **AC6 — Telegraphing:** Each attack phase begins with clear tell animations and advance audio cues (≥ 500 ms lead time) before the visual event.
- [ ] **AC7 — All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Engine:** Phaser v4 + TypeScript.
- **Gym scope:** This scene is a standalone gym scene (not shipped with the game) — no player ship, no other enemy types, no HUD beyond health bar, no power-ups.
- **Enemy behaviour:** The Boss is multi-hit (4 phases). Each phase has a distinct visual representation and attack pattern.
- **Phase transitions:** Visual cues (core exposure, brightness) indicate phase progression. Audio cues announce transitions.
- **Firing:** All Boss attack phases fire complex bullet patterns. Patterns should be learnable but increasingly difficult as phases progress.
- **Audio:** Play distinct sound effects for spawn, each phase's unique audio cue, phase transitions, and destruction.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` — The Boss gym scene.
- `src/entities/Boss.ts` — Boss enemy entity (multi-phase health + attack patterns).
- `src/assets/` — Boss sprite (large, imposing neon entity with core).
- `src/audio/` — Boss-related sound effects (spawn, phase cues, transitions, destruction).

## Related work

- **Create E1 Scout gym scene (AH-0MT994ESD000RP1Q)** — related; implements V-formation pattern.
- **Refactor Enemy Gym Scenes (AH-0MT985FOA008JWM9)** — related; will refactor code across enemy gym scenes.
- **Gym index scene (AH-0MT985VRY009JXLZ)** — related; will link to this scene from the gym index.
- **Game Design Document (AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5)** — authoritative spec, §4.3 Boss Design (The Central AI).

## Best practices (mandatory — see docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md)

This scene MUST be built on the shared core gym formation-scene library and follow the conventions documented in **`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`** (see §3 "Best practice: adding a new enemy gym scene" and §5 "Extending the core library"). In particular:

- Extend `GymFormationScene` (src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts) wherever the scene is a formation-driven gym scene; supply only entity-specific configuration (`EnemyFormationConfig`), constants, and thin test accessors — DO NOT copy the ~200-line formation/UI/bullet boilerplate from the pre-refactor `GymScout`/`GymDiver`/`GymTank`.
- Movement that exceeds `applyFormationPosition()`'s flat-translation contract (e.g. E4 orbital paths, E5 clusters, Boss phases) belongs in the **entity** or as a new seam in the core library per §5 — never by duplicating scene boilerplate.
- Reuse the shared formation-offset builders in `src/utils/formations.ts` for any grid/formation geometry; add new pure builders there with unit tests.
- Follow the new-scene checklist: `add.existing()` for display-list membership, `lineStyle()` after `clear()` in entity drawing, exported tuning constants, test accessors, and per-scene tests (spawn count, geometry, drift, EXPLODE, SHOOT toggle, `← INDEX`).
- Update `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §1/§3 if this scene introduces a new convention.

- [ ] **AC9 — Core library reuse:** The scene extends the shared `GymFormationScene` core library or its documented extension seam (§5 of `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`) where applicable (Boss phase/health extensions may compose with the base class) and contains no duplicated formation/UI/bullet boilerplate.
- [ ] **AC10 — Guide compliance:** The implementation follows `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §3–§5: `add.existing()`, `lineStyle()` after `clear()`, exported constants, test accessors, and per-scene tests.

# Create gym scene for non-combat power-ups (P5 Speed Boost, P8 Extra Life, P9 Magnet) with round-robin spawning, collection, and standalone power-up HUD

## Problem statement

The gym suite (GymIndex + per-mechanic scenes) currently has no scene demonstrating power-up spawning, collection, and HUD feedback: the existing gym scenes explicitly exclude HUD and power-ups. This item adds a single `GymPowerUps` scene (auto-discovered by the gym index) that cycles through the **non-weapon, non-combat** power-ups **P5 Speed Boost, P8 Extra Life, P9 Magnet** round-robin — each spawns every 5 s, grows from nothing to full size, sits stationary for 5 s, shrinks to nothing and despawns — while the player ship flies around collecting them. Collected power-ups apply their **full behaviour** (observable without threats) and their states (timers, stack counts, lives) are rendered by a **standalone HUD class** designed to be attachable to any Phaser scene.

> **Scope boundary (per operator, three-way split):**
> - **Weapon power-ups** (P1 Spread Shot, P2 Rapid Fire + new weapon patterns) → sibling **AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR** ("Weapon power-ups (3 patterns + reset) with auto-fire and weapon gym scene", in-progress).
> - **Combat-coupled power-ups** (P3 Shield, P4 Bomb, P6 Phase Shift, P7 Teleport — full behaviour demonstrable only with threats) → sibling **AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40** ("Create combat gym scene for combat-coupled power-ups… with low-level enemy threats").
> - **This item = non-combat, threat-free gym: P5, P8, P9**, plus the shared spawn/lifecycle mechanics, ship, and the standalone HUD class (the combat scene depends on this item for those reusable pieces).

## Users

- **Player / developer testing the game** — wants to see each non-combat power-up spawn, grow, sit, shrink, and fade in isolation, and to verify collection + effect application + HUD feedback feel right before any combat is added.
- **AI agents / developers implementing AI_Hell** — need a reusable power-up lifecycle (spawn/grow/hold/shrink/collect), per-type effect behaviour, and a standalone HUD that any future scene (main game, other gyms, the combat gym) can attach.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want to fly over a grown power-up to collect it, so I can see its effect take hold (e.g., a faster ship, a lives bump, drops drifting toward me) and watch it appear on the HUD.
- As a **player**, I want the HUD to show the active power-ups with remaining timers (timed types) and counts (stackable/permanent types), so I always know what is currently active.
- As a **developer**, I want re-collecting a timed power-up to refresh its timer to the full duration, so repeated pickups behave predictably.
- As a **developer**, I want the HUD to be a standalone class any scene can instantiate, so the main game and the combat gym don't have to re-implement power-up status UI.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Single gym scene with ship:** A new `GymPowerUps` scene (key `GymPowerUps`, label `PowerUps`) is defined in `src/scenes/gym/`, auto-discovered and listed by the gym index, boots correctly, renders the player ship with the standard thrust movement + screen-wrap from `GymPlayer`, and has the shared "← INDEX" back button.
- [ ] **AC2 — Round-robin spawn/lifecycle:** The scene spawns exactly the non-combat power-ups **P5, P8, P9 in ascending GDD order (P5 Speed Boost, P8 Extra Life, P9 Magnet)**, one every 5 s, each remaining stationary for a 5 s lifetime. On spawn the drop **grows from scale 0 to full size**; on despawn it **shrinks to nothing** then is removed; growth/shrink are delta-time driven (framerate-independent) and the window durations are tunable constants.
- [ ] **AC3 — Collection rule:** A drop is collectible only while its current scale is **> 3% of full size** (i.e., during grow, full-size hold, and shrink until it drops below the threshold); collecting requires the ship to overlap the drop. A drop that fades uncollected is removed with no effect.
- [ ] **AC4 — Full per-type behaviour (threat-free):** Collecting each type applies its full GDD §4.4 behaviour as observable without threats: **P5 Speed Boost** — +50% movement speed (thrust/max-speed) applied live to the ship's movement for 10 s; **P8 Extra Life** — +1 life immediately (cap 5, excess ignored), reflected in the HUD lives counter (starting at 3); **P9 Magnet** — permanent effect, one stack per pickup (cap 5), radius 2× ship size +50% per stack, attracting on-screen power-up drops toward the ship at a speed slower than the ship's max speed.
- [ ] **AC5 — Timer refresh:** Re-collecting an already-active timed power-up (P5) refreshes its timer to the full duration (not additive, not ignored). Permanent/passive types follow their own rules (P9 stacks to cap 5 then no-op; P8 excess ignored above cap 5).
- [ ] **AC6 — Standalone HUD class:** A standalone `src/ui/HUD.ts` class (Phaser game-object based, attachable to any scene, rendered above gameplay) shows, for each active power-up: **icon, name, and either a remaining-seconds timer (timed types) or a stack/pickup count (P9 magnet stacks)**, plus the **lives count** (P8). The gym scene uses this HUD; the class contains no gym-specific logic and is reusable by the combat gym scene (AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40).
- [ ] **AC7 — Testing/validation:** Unit tests cover: spawn timing + round-robin order, grow/shrink lifecycle, the 3% collection threshold, effect timers + refresh semantics, P8 cap, P9 stacking cap + attraction math, and the HUD's model (timer/count/lives aggregation, scene-attachability). Scene-level tests (gameHarness) verify discovery, ship presence, collection, and back button. Full suite green.
- [ ] **AC8 — Documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (GDD §6.4 architecture gains the `GymPowerUps` scene and `ui/HUD.ts` power-up panel entries).
- [ ] **AC9 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Engine/stack:** Phaser v4 + TypeScript, Vite, Vitest (locked). Neon-vector aesthetic; code-drawn graphics only — **no external art assets**; icons are code-drawn per GDD §4.4 icon suggestions.
- **Scope:** this gym is threat-free (no enemies, no enemy bullets). Weapon power-ups (P1/P2 + new weapon patterns) belong to AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR; combat-coupled types (P3/P4/P6/P7) belong to AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40.
- **Spawn cadence:** one spawn every 5 s; 5 s lifetime → exactly one drop on screen at any time (spawn of the next coincides with despawn of the previous), round-robin over P5 → P8 → P9 then repeat.
- **HUD reusability:** the HUD must be a standalone class attachable to any scene — it must not import or depend on gym-only code (the combat gym depends on it).
- **Collection geometry:** overlap-based (drop radius + ship hull radius), gated by the 3% scale threshold.
- **Growth/shrink windows:** default 0.5 s grow / 0.5 s shrink inside the 5 s lifetime (tunable constants in `src/core/constants.ts`), leaving ~4 s at full size.
- **Re-collection:** timed effects refresh to full duration (operator decision Q5; captured in AC5).

## Existing state

- Gym infrastructure exists: `GymIndex` (auto-discovery via `import.meta.glob` on `src/scenes/gym/*.ts`, labels, "← INDEX" nav via `src/utils/gymNavigation.ts`), base formation scene (`src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`), and scenes `GymPlayer`, `GymScout`, `GymDiver`, `GymTank` — all explicitly "no HUD, no power-ups".
- Player ship + thrust movement exist (`src/entities/Player.ts`, `src/utils/movement.ts`, `GymPlayer.ts`) with live-tunable config (`src/core/config.ts`).
- **No power-up or HUD code exists** in `src/` (no `powerups/` nor `ui/HUD.ts` yet). GDD §4.4 defines P1–P9 semantics and icon suggestions; GDD §6.4 architecture plans `powerups/` and `ui/HUD.ts`.
- Sibling AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR (in-progress) covers weapon power-ups with its own weapon gym scene, using the same spawn/grow/shrink/3%-collection mechanics (7 s lifetime there).
- Sibling AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40 (new, depends on this item) covers the combat-coupled power-ups P3/P4/P6/P7 in a combat gym scene with E1 Scout threats.
- Tests use Vitest + a gameHarness (`src/test/gameHarness.ts`) with happy-dom; `Scout` entity (`src/entities/Scout.ts`) provides `tryFireAimedBullet`, formation offsets and destroy lifecycle for the sibling combat scene.

## Desired change

1. Add `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUps.ts` — single scene: ship (reused `Player` + movement), round-robin power-up spawner (P5 → P8 → P9, one per 5 s), grow/hold/shrink lifecycle, overlap collection gated at scale > 3%, per-type effect application (P5/P8/P9), HUD attachment, back button.
2. Add a power-up implementation under `src/powerups/` (base lifecycle class + type catalogue for the non-combat types; icon drawing) — following the GDD §6.4 layout (`PowerUp.ts` base etc.), kept in a form reusable by the main game and the combat gym, which extends the catalogue with P3/P4/P6/P7 entries and threat-coupled effect hooks.
3. Add `src/ui/HUD.ts` — standalone class attachable to any scene, rendering above gameplay (Phaser Container + text): active power-up icons, names, timers/counts, and lives.
4. Add constants for the spawn/lifecycle tuning to `src/core/constants.ts`.
5. Update the GDD §6.4 architecture briefly (list `GymPowerUps`; note `ui/HUD.ts` power-up panel as implemented).
6. Tests: unit tests for lifecycle/timing/round-robin/threshold/effects/magnet/HUD model + scene tests via gameHarness.

## Key Files:

- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUps.ts` — **new** gym scene (the deliverable).
- `src/powerups/PowerUp.ts` — **new** base power-up class (spawn/grow/hold/shrink/collect lifecycle).
- `src/powerups/types.ts` (or `PowerUpTypes.ts`) — **new** power-up catalogue (P5/P8/P9 entries here; P3/P4/P6/P7 entries added by the combat-gym item): id, name, icon, duration/stack semantics per GDD §4.4.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — **new** active-effects registry: timers, lives, live movement multiplier (P5), magnet attractor (P9).
- `src/powerups/icons.ts` — **new** code-drawn neon icons per GDD §4.4 suggestions (used by both field drops and HUD).
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — **new** standalone HUD class (attachable to any scene; icons/timers/counts/lives).
- `src/core/constants.ts` — spawn interval, lifetime, grow/shrink windows, collection threshold (3%), sizing constants.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUps.test.ts` (+ power-up/effect/HUD unit tests) — **new** tests.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §6.4 architecture: add `GymPowerUps`, note `ui/HUD.ts` power-up panel implemented.

## Related work

- **AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40** — "Create combat gym scene for combat-coupled power-ups… with low-level enemy threats": sibling that **depends on this item** (reuses the power-up lifecycle + catalogue + HUD) and adds the combat-coupled types P3/P4/P6/P7 with E1 Scout threats. Dependency edge: combat-gym → this item.
- **AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR** — "Weapon power-ups (3 patterns + reset) with auto-fire and weapon gym scene" (in-progress): sibling gym for weapon power-ups; same round-robin/grow/shrink/3%-collection mechanics with a 7 s lifetime; sets the scope boundary (weapon types excluded here). Related-to (shared lifecycle mechanics, complementary scope) — should not drift apart.
- **GymPlayer scene** — ship movement/input pattern reused by this scene.
- **"Create gym scene with player ship and thrust-based space movement" (AH-0MT97OA3E001DOYW)** — the player gym; precedent for `Player` reuse.
- **"Refactor Enemy Gym Scenes" (AH-0MT987VA3005YBNK) + core library (AH-0MTAN4IFR007U9B3)** — the shared gym base-class pattern (buttons, back button, discovery exclusions) this scene should follow.
- GDD power-up catalog items (completed): "Add an extra life power up" (AH-0MT7UX8LE0072MR3), "Add a Magnet power up" (AH-0MT7VE4SX0005A8V) — semantics source for P8/P9.
- GDD items (completed): "Game Design Document for AI_Hell" (AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — non-combat split:** combat-coupled power-ups (P3/P4/P6/P7) were removed from this item per operator direction (see Appendix Q7/Q8); this item covers P5/P8/P9 only and provides the shared lifecycle/HUD the combat scene depends on.
- **Assumption — P8 lives counter:** the HUD lives counter starts at 3 and increments on P8 collection (cap 5) exactly as the GDD lives model; no hits occur in this threat-free gym, so lives are never lost here.
- **Assumption — growth/shrink windows:** 0.5 s grow / 0.5 s shrink (tunable) inside the 5 s lifetime; collection allowed whenever scale > 3% (roughly the whole window except the first/last moments).
- **Assumption — icons:** code-drawn neon icons per GDD §4.4 suggestions, consistent with the code-first/no-asset convention; shared between field drops and HUD.
- **Scope-creep guard:** weapon power-ups, combat-coupled power-ups, enemy/bullet threat sources, score display, main-menu HUD variants, and gameplay-scene integration are out of scope; record any extras as linked work items.
- **Risk — sibling divergence:** both sibling gyms (weapon AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR, combat AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40) use the same spawn cadence/3% mechanics; if they land first with different constants or a shared lifecycle module, coordinate to avoid divergent implementations (extract a shared lifecycle util if needed).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (round 1): "Should there be a single `GymPowerUps` scene that cycles through all power-up types, or separate gym scenes per type?" — Answer (operator): **"1. single"** — one scene cycles all types round-robin. Source: interactive reply.
- Q2 (round 1): "Which power-up types should the gym cover — all 9 or a subset?" — Answer (operator): **"2. all of them"** — subsequently split three ways (see Q4/Q6/Q7): weapons → AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR; combat-coupled → AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40; here = P5/P8/P9. Source: interactive reply.
- Q3 (round 1): "For the standalone HUD, what should it display and should it be a Phaser scene or DOM overlay?" — Answer (operator): **"Active effect timers, collection counts as applicable for stackable items, icons. Your call re phaser scene vs overlay as long as it can be displayed over another schene [scene]."** — Research: no HUD code exists; `GymPlayer` uses a DOM overlay, gym scenes use Phaser text/graphics; a Phaser game-object class attachable to any scene (Container above gameplay) fits the neon aesthetic and the existing harness. Decision: standalone `src/ui/HUD.ts` class, Phaser-side, attachable to any scene.
- Q4 (round 2): "Combat-only power-ups (P1/P2/P4/P6/P7) — implement full behaviour in the gym or register-only timers?" — Answer (operator): **"Do not include weapon power ups in this gym scene (there is another work item for those), any powerups that are present in this scene should implement full behaviour."** — Research: `wl search weapon` found **AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR** (in-progress "Weapon power-ups (3 patterns + reset) with auto-fire and weapon gym scene"). Final accepted: weapon power-ups excluded (sibling item); all power-ups present here implement full behaviour.
- Q5 (round 2): "Re-collecting an already-active timed power-up — reset timer to full duration (refresh) or ignore?" — Answer (operator): **"2. refresh"** — timer refreshes to full duration. Source: interactive reply.
- Q6 (round 3): "Shield/Bomb/PhaseShift/Teleport full behaviour needs threats to demonstrate. Add a minimal threat source (e.g., bullet-spawn button) or keep the gym threat-free?" — Answer (operator): **"There are no threats. There is another work item to create a gym for other power ups."** — Final accepted (round 4, scope split): the combat-coupled power-ups (P3/P4/P6/P7) were pulled out of this item into the new combat gym scene item AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40; threat sources live there. This item keeps the threat-free types P5/P8/P9. Second answer (this round): **"Just use scout (with shooting)"** — the combat scene's threat is an E1 Scout formation with shooting enabled. Sources: interactive replies.
- Q7 (round 4): "Which enemies constitute 'low level enemy threats' — reuse existing E1 Scout/E2 Diver/E3 Tank entities with bullet-firing, or generic placeholders?" — Answer (operator): **"1. Just use scout (with shooting)"** — the combat scene uses the existing E1 Scout entity with its aimed bullet-firing. Source: interactive reply.
- Q8 (round 4): "Ship hit response in the combat gym — (a) lives with respawn (3 lives), (b) simple flash/reset without a lives counter, (c) other?" — Answer (operator): **"2. b"** — simple flash/reset, no lives counter (pure demo). Source: interactive reply. Note: this affects the combat gym only; this item's P8 lives counter remains display-only (no hit model here).

- **AH-0MT9FS3DL0084Z6V** – Gym scene: ship config sliders, save button, half-speed ship (completed)
- **AH-0MTAF76Q1008BLBE** – Direction-neutral ship shape: circle with engines at top, bottom, and each side (in-progress)

# Create combat gym scene for combat-coupled power-ups (P3 Shield, P4 Bomb, P6 Phase Shift, P7 Teleport) with low-level enemy threats

## Problem statement

Four power-up types in the GDD catalogue — **P3 Shield, P4 Bomb, P6 Phase Shift, P7 Teleport** — cannot demonstrate their full behaviour without threats: Shield must absorb a hit, Bomb must clear on-screen enemy bullets, Phase Shift must pass through enemies and bullets, and Teleport must search for a safe spot free of threats. The operator split these "combat-coupled" types out of the threat-free power-up gym (AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT) into this dedicated **combat gym scene** that contains a **low-level enemy threat (E1 Scout with shooting)**. The scene shares the round-robin spawn lifecycle, grow-shrink animation, 3% collection threshold, player ship, and standalone HUD class with the non-combat gym, on which this item depends.

## Users

- **Player / developer testing the game** — wants to see each combat-coupled power-up's full effect against real (but low-level) threats: a shield bubble popping on a hit, a bomb wiping a bullet cloud, ghosting straight through a formation, and blinking away to a safe spot.
- **AI agents / developers implementing AI_Hell** — need the threat-coupled behaviour (hit absorption, bullet clearing, intangibility, safe-spot resolution) implemented and tested once, in a form the main game can reuse.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want my shield bubble to absorb exactly one hit and pop, so I can verify the GDD's "absorbs one hit" rule.
- As a **player**, I want to collect a Bomb while scouts are firing and see every on-screen enemy bullet vanish, with enemies untouched (they are 1 HP, GDD §4.4).
- As a **player**, I want Phase Shift to let me fly straight through the scout formation and its bullets without being hit, for 3 seconds.
- As a **player**, I want to press Space with a collected Teleport to jump to the nearest safe spot (free of scouts and bullets) along my travel direction, gaining Phase Shift on arrival.
- As a **developer**, I want the ship's hit response (no shield/phase shift) to be a simple flash/reset with no lives counter, so the demo keeps a pure combat focus.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Combat scene with ship + low-level threats:** A new `GymPowerUpsCombat` scene (key `GymPowerUpsCombat`, label `PowerUps Combat`) is defined in `src/scenes/gym/`, auto-discovered and listed by the gym index, boots correctly, renders the player ship with standard thrust movement + screen-wrap, and contains a **formation of E1 Scout enemies** (reusing `src/entities/Scout.ts` + the formation utilities) with a **SHOOT toggle** that enables aimed enemy fire at the **ship's live position** (not the fixed demo target), so hits are demonstrable. Shared "← INDEX" back button present.
- [ ] **AC2 — Round-robin spawn/lifecycle:** The scene spawns exactly the combat-coupled power-ups **P3, P4, P6, P7 in ascending GDD order**, one every 5 s, each remaining stationary for a 5 s lifetime; spawn = **grow from scale 0 to full size**, despawn = **shrink to nothing**; growth/shrink delta-time driven with the same tunable constants as the non-combat gym (AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT).
- [ ] **AC3 — Collection rule:** A drop is collectible only while its current scale is **> 3% of full size** (grow, hold, and shrink until below threshold); collection requires the ship to overlap the drop; an uncollected drop fades with no effect.
- [ ] **AC4 — P3 Shield full behaviour:** Collecting P3 arms a shield bubble rendered around the ship for **15 s**; the bubble **absorbs exactly one hit** (enemy body or enemy bullet) and then pops (effect ends, no ship flash/reset for that hit); if never hit, it expires after 15 s. Re-collection while active refreshes the timer to 15 s.
- [ ] **AC5 — P4 Bomb full behaviour:** Collecting P4 instantly removes **all on-screen enemy bullets** (aimed scout fire in-flight), does **not damage enemies** (GDD §4.4 note), is not a timed effect, and shows a brief HUD notice. Re-collection while enemies are not firing is a benign no-op (bullets cleared anyway).
- [ ] **AC6 — P6 Phase Shift full behaviour:** Collecting P6 renders a ghost-outline ship for **3 s** during which the ship **passes through enemy bodies and enemy bullets without being hit**; hit checks are disabled for the duration. Re-collection refreshes the timer to 3 s.

- [ ] **AC8 — Hit response (no shield/phase shift):** Being hit by an enemy body or enemy bullet with no active P3/P6 triggers a **simple flash/reset with no lives counter** (e.g., brief invulnerability + reposition), per operator decision; this is the only consequence — no lives, no game over.

# Add player to each Enemy Gym scene (AH-0MTD0Z0Y7003T1NT)

## Problem statement

The five enemy gym scenes — E1 Scout (`GymScout`), E2 Diver (`GymDiver`), E3 Tank
(`GymTank`), E4 Phaser (`GymPhaser`), E5 Swarm (`GymSwarm`) — contain **no player
ship**: enemies aim, fire, and dive at a fixed bottom-centre stand-in position
(documented as "standing in for the player"). Add the real, keyboard-controlled
`Player` ship to each scene with live combat interaction, so the enemy behaviour
is demonstrated against an actual target and the scenes double as combat
testbeds.

## Users

- **Developers / AI agents implementing AI_Hell** — want enemy-gym scenes that
  demonstrate enemy AI against the real player ship, with working combat
  feedback (hits, deaths, explosions), so behaviour can be verified in context.

### Example user stories

- As a **developer**, I want the Scout's aimed shots and the Diver's dive to
  track the *actual* player position, so I can verify L4+ behaviours against a
  moving target.
- As a **developer**, I want to fly the player ship (arrows + WASD) through each
  enemy gym, auto-firing, so I can test that player bullets destroy enemies
  (with explosion VFX/SFX) and enemy bullets hit the ship (explosion + respawn,
  infinite lives).
- As a **developer**, I want the closest-approach enemy bullets destroyed by
  player bullets, so fire-and-forget aiming feels responsive.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Player in every enemy gym scene:** `GymScout`, `GymDiver`,
  `GymTank`, `GymPhaser`, `GymSwarm` each spawn the existing `Player` ship
  (keyboard-controlled via arrows + WASD, using the shared input/movement
  plumbing), and the gym index still boots all five scenes.
- [ ] **AC2 — Live aim tracking:** enemy aimed fire (Scout shots, Diver dive,
  Swarm coordinated bursts, Phaser patterns per its telegraph rules) targets the
  player's current position each frame instead of the fixed bottom-centre
  stand-in. Tank radial burst (direction-agnostic) is unchanged.
- [ ] **AC3 — Combat interaction:** player auto-fires in the direction of travel
  (GDD §2.3, default Cannon, as in `GymWeapons`); player bullets destroy enemies
  (existing `destroySelf()` explosion VFX + SFX) and destroy enemy bullets.
- [ ] **AC4 — Player hit / respawn:** an enemy bullet hitting the player plays
  hit VFX + SFX and re-spawns the ship (explosion, brief re-spawn with
  invulnerability blink — infinite lives, no game-over state, no score change).
- [ ] **AC5 — Existing controls preserved:** the `EXPLODE` and `SHOOT: ON/OFF`
  HUD buttons remain; `SHOOT` keeps toggling enemy firing (L4+ simulation).
- [ ] **AC6 — Testing:** automated tests cover player spawn/control, live aim
  tracking, player-bullet ↔ enemy/bullet collisions, enemy-bullet → player hit +
  respawn (with invulnerability), and that existing scene behaviour is preserved;
  full project test suite passes.
- [ ] **AC7 — Docs:** `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` updated to
  document the player-in-enemy-gym convention (spawn, input, collisions,
  respawn); all related documentation updated to reflect the changes.

## Constraints

- Scenes are demonstration-only: **no game-over**, no lives counter, no scoring
  changes, no pause/level progression.
- Boss gym scene (**AH-0MT99QBDW001O7PE**) is **out of scope** — it does not
  exist yet and is tracked separately.
- Prefer extending the shared core library (`core/GymFormationScene.ts`) over
  per-scene boilerplate; keep the `EnemyFormationConfig` contract backward

  `EnemyFormationConfig` extensions.
